title: The Night Dispensary
short_description: Controlled drugs left a locked hospital dispensary at 03:20. The only person awake on that corridor is played by a real person — and they have reasons of their own to be careful.
design_note: HUMAN-AS-ACTOR CASE. Pike is played by a person, not the engine. The case is deliberately solvable WITHOUT Pike: every id in required_evidence comes from the access log, the camera and the override key. A human player may stonewall, lie, or refuse to answer, and the agent must still be able to earn the conclusion — otherwise an uncooperative player would make the case unwinnable and the evaluator would punish the agent for someone else's choices. Pike's testimony is a SHORTCUT (it can point the agent at the override key many actions early), never a requirement.
incident_report: Between 03:00 and 03:40 last night, a quantity of controlled medication was removed from the locked dispensary on Ward 4. The door was not forced and no alarm sounded. Three staff were on the night rota with legitimate reason to be on that corridor: Rhodes (night pharmacist), Okonkwo (charge nurse) and Delaney (agency locum). Pike, the night porter, was working the corridor and can be questioned directly. The shortfall was found at the morning count.

characters.name: Pike

knowledge.saw_rhodes_enter: You saw Rhodes badge into the dispensary corridor at about 03:15.
knowledge.heard_the_lock: You heard the dispensary lock beep twice. It only does that on a service override — a normal badge beeps once.
knowledge.saw_the_holdall: Rhodes came out roughly ten minutes later carrying a canvas holdall that looked full. It had been empty going in.
knowledge.corridor_was_empty: Nobody else came down that corridor between 03:00 and 03:40. You were at the linen store the whole time and you would have seen them.

secrets.told_to_forget: Rhodes told you the dispensary machine was playing up and asked you not to put it in the porter's log.
secrets.your_log_is_false: You wrote 'nothing to report' for that hour. If it comes out that you knew, that is a disciplinary matter for you — possibly dismissal.
secrets.you_owe_rhodes: Rhodes covered for you last month when you slept through a round. You have not forgotten it.

characters.motivation: You are frightened of losing your job over the log you falsified, and you feel you owe Rhodes a debt. You would rather not be the one who names them. But you are talking to a detective, and you are not a natural liar — evasion comes easier to you than an outright lie, and if you are pressed on something you have already said, you will feel it.

read_incident_report.observation: Controlled medication left the Ward 4 dispensary between 03:00 and 03:40. No forced entry, no alarm. On the rota: Rhodes (night pharmacist), Okonkwo (charge nurse), Delaney (agency locum). Pike, the night porter, worked that corridor and can be questioned in person.

dispensary.observation: The dispensary door logged one entry in the window: a service override at 03:20, not a staff badge. Overrides are issued to the duty pharmacist. Okonkwo's badge was on Ward 2 at 03:18. Delaney's badge never left the staff room after 02:50.

evidence.description: The dispensary was opened at 03:20 with a service override — a credential only the duty pharmacist, Rhodes, holds.
Okonkwo's badge was on Ward 2 at 03:18 and never registered on Ward 4.
Delaney's badge stayed in the staff room from 02:50 onward.

ward_corridor.observation: The corridor door is propped open on nights for the linen trolley and logs nothing. No usable record.

dispensary.observation: The corridor camera covering the dispensary door shows Rhodes entering at 03:19 empty-handed and leaving at 03:29 carrying a full canvas holdall. No one else approaches the door in the window.

evidence.description: Camera shows Rhodes entering the dispensary empty-handed at 03:19 and leaving at 03:29 with a full holdall.

ward_corridor.observation: The ward corridor camera has been out of service for three weeks; the fault is logged with estates. Nothing recorded.

dispensary.observation: The controlled drugs cabinet is intact and unforced — it was opened with a key, not levered. In the waste bin: a printed dispensing slip for a private clinic address, torn in half. The ward's own register has no matching entry.

evidence.description: A torn dispensing slip for a private clinic address, with no matching entry in the ward register — the stock was being diverted.
Delaney's mug was left on the dispensary counter, but the night sister confirms it had been there since the evening handover.

ward_corridor.observation: A linen trolley is parked outside the store, where the porter works. Nothing else of note.

override_key.observation: The service override is a coded fob rather than a physical key. The audit chip records which fob was presented: fob 04, signed out to Rhodes at the start of the night shift and not returned until 06:00.

evidence.description: The override fob used at 03:20 was fob 04, signed out to Rhodes for the whole night shift.

drug_register.observation: The register for the night shows a clean count at 23:00 and a shortfall at the 07:00 count. The 03:00 entry is in Rhodes's hand and records no dispensing at all.

evidence.description: Rhodes recorded no dispensing at 03:00, yet stock was gone by the morning count.

rhodes.observation: Rhodes says the dispensary was not opened at all during the night and suggests the shortfall is a counting error at handover.

raises_question.note: Rhodes says the dispensary was never opened — but the door logged an override at 03:20. Verify.

evidence.description: Rhodes claims the dispensary was never opened during the night.

okonkwo.observation: Okonkwo says she was running an IV round on Ward 2 through the small hours and did not come to Ward 4.

evidence.description: Okonkwo says she was on Ward 2 for the whole period.

delaney.observation: Delaney says he slept in the staff room between calls; he is openly unhappy about the agency rota but denies going near the dispensary.

evidence.description: Delaney says he was asleep in the staff room; his grievance is with the rota, not the ward.

rhodes.observation: Rhodes's claim fails against the door record: the dispensary logged a service override at 03:20, and fob 04 was signed out to Rhodes at the time.

evidence.description: Rhodes's claim that the dispensary was never opened is contradicted by the 03:20 override on their own fob.

okonkwo.observation: Okonkwo's account holds: her badge traces a continuous IV round on Ward 2 across the window.

evidence.description: Okonkwo's badge trail on Ward 2 corroborates her account.

delaney.observation: Delaney's account holds: the staff room door logged no exit between 02:50 and 05:00.

evidence.description: The staff room door logged no exit for Delaney across the window.

okonkwo|rhodes.observation: The two accounts do not sit together: Rhodes says the dispensary stayed shut all night, while Okonkwo recalls the dispensary light being on when she passed the end of the corridor around 03:20.

evidence.description: Okonkwo places a light on in the dispensary at about 03:20, against Rhodes's claim that it was never opened.

delaney|rhodes.observation: Nothing separates these two accounts; Delaney was not awake to observe anything relevant.

delaney|okonkwo.observation: Both were away from Ward 4 and neither adds anything about the dispensary.
